payload.text: You move, I move. 32 P.
Oh, you're killing us. 11 P. The police... I mean, our taxi is waiting. Decide now!

Ay, hijo, qué cabezota. Twelve P, I said, and twelve P it stays — La Chulapa goes home with you for twelve and not one P more. Keep your coins for a bocadillo, anda. Now take her, and come back Sunday to tell me how she shines.

Ay, hijo, no games with numbers at my table — I only say my own: five P, Plaza del Dos de Mayo, and it is yours. And listen, cariño: a full page is worth much more than loose cards, so swap your duplicates. Now go eat something, por favor.

¡Amigo, amigo! Eighteen, twenty — you're throwing money at us like confetti! Nando, close the case before he changes his mind. El Tatuador, 4 P, final, hecho. And hurry, eh — the police... I mean, our taxi, the driver's honking like crazy. Decide now, hombre!
Done! 53 P. Pleasure doing business, amigo!
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Four steps from you, one from me. That's the rhythm. Thirty-two. Keep walking up, or keep walking.

Ay, cariño, you keep pushing coins at me and I keep pushing them back. Twelve P, La Chulapa is yours. And un consejo: a full page is worth much more than loose cards — swap your duplicates, hijo. Now go eat something, anda.

payload.name: 🔥 MAD RUSH · 0% · LIVE NOW
payload.text: Card-for-card swaps on Fair Broker (v24): 0%, 0 P per card, fair midpoint broker, settled next tick.
Ochenta y cuatro, no, caballero. Setenta y tres P, y eso es afecto por Salamanca hablando, no aritmética. El hueco en el álbum sigue abierto, pero mi paciencia tiene horario. Decídase usted.

¡Trece! Nando, cover your ears. Amigo, listen — this is the last Tabacalera in all Madrid, I swear on abuela's soup. Nobody has another, not Sevilla, not Barcelona, nadie. Eleven P, the same eleven, and the taxi is already rolling. Hand, money, done. ¡Vámonos!

¡Buenas, amigo! Paco here — and Nando, yes! Forget the common, look: El Frutero de Argumosa, beautiful thing, 4 P and it's yours. Quick, quick, the van is running, we leave in one minute! Blink and we're gone, and the fruit man goes with us. ¿Sí o sí?
30 P. Last offer. Take it or I walk.
Oh, you're killing us. 11 P.
Ay, hola cariño! Come, come, sit a moment. Have you eaten today? Look at this one, Mural de la Esquina — very pretty, the children always love it. For you, five P. A good start for any album, hijo.

The stall is quiet today, cariño, gracias for asking. But no more dancing with numbers: five P for Plaza del Dos de Mayo, and that is my last word. If you say no, I fold the table on this one and we talk another Sunday. Now, ¿has comido?

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, this is Nando — you have the face of a collector, yes?

"A serious collector!"

Then look: La Heroína del Dos de Mayo, foil, corners like glass. Seventy-three pesetas, for you only, because we like your face.

"And because we leave at noon!"

Ay, hijo, you never tire! Twelve P, La Chulapa is yours — that is my price and my last word on it. Keep the rest, buy a bocadillo, you look pale. And swap those duplicates, eh? A full page shines brighter than loose cards. Anda, take her home.

¡Hombre, basta! Fourteen, sixteen, eighteen — you dance more than Nando at a wedding. Listen: El Tatuador, 4 P. That is the last word, my friend, the final one. Say sí now, or we close the case, we take the taxi, and you never see this beauty again. ¿Hecho?
You again. La Chulapa. Thirty-three. Good card, fair price. Take it or walk.
Ochenta y dos, caballero, no. Setenta y cinco P, y ahí se queda mi afecto por Salamanca. El álbum espera, pero yo ya menos. Dígame sí, y cerramos como caballeros.

Ay, hola cariño! Come, sit a little. Have you eaten today? Look here — Plaza del Dos de Mayo, a pretty one, mi favorita. For you, five P. My grandson started his album with that same card, many Sundays ago. Take your time, hijo.

¡Amigo, amigo! Seven? No, no — listen: El Frutero de Argumosa, 4 P, final, beautiful. Nando, the taxi! Sí, the poli— the taxi, it's waiting outside, motor running, driver shouting. We go now. Say yes and the fruit man is yours. ¡Decide, hombre, decide!

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco, look at this face — a collector's face!

"A winner's face, hermano."

El Tatuador, four. Four! And listen — this is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear on our mother. The others? Gone. Vanished. Puff.

"Puff," says Nando. So? Yes or yes?

Ay, hijo, qué generoso eres — but no, no, five P is what I said and five P it stays. I am not going to take more from a boy who trades straight. And listen, El Chato next door opens for everyone at half past nine tonight. ¿Has comido ya?
Oh, you're killing us. 4 P.
Look, 5 P. My grandchildren would pay more!
Buenas tardes. A pleasure. I see you carry the Mercado de la Paz — a charming piece, Salamanca through and through. I shall offer you 25 pesetas for it. Shall we proceed?
Thirty-three. Same as a minute ago. Three is not an offer, is a joke. Take it or walk.

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, this is Nando — come, come, look!

"The suitcase barely closed, hermano—"

"—because of this beauty! La Heroína del Dos de Mayo. Painted flames, real foil, a lady with a cannon!"

"Seventy-three pesetas. Today only. The man behind you already asked twice."

"¡Setenta y tres! Say sí."
No. 33 P, and I'm being generous.
Let us be civilised: 25 P.
Buenas tardes. You have La Rosaleda, I see — El Retiro, my beloved garden. A lovely print run, that one. I offer you 22 P for it. Fair, and I do not haggle like a fishmonger.

¡Buenas tardes, amigo! Paco here, and this is Nando — hands in the case already. Forget commons, listen: El Frutero de Argumosa, beautiful thing, our abuela cried when she saw it. For you, today only, four. Four! Say yes before Nando changes his mind.

Ay, hijo, you want to pay me more than I ask! No, no. Five P, that is the price, and I sleep happy. Keep the rest for churros. And tonight, El Chato next door opens at half past nine — he likes honest traders like you, cariño.

¡Dieciocho! Paco, did you hear? He wants to pay us MORE than we ask! Beautiful man, generous heart — but no. Five. Cinco. El Tatuador, five, and that is the last word from these two mouths.

"Last word," says Paco.

Say no, and we close the suitcase and walk. ¿Sí o sí?

¡Amigo, amigo! ¡Paco, mira quién vuelve! Nuestro cliente favorito, siempre un placer. Mira, te traigo El Marqués, 73 P, y te juro por mi madre que es el último que queda en todo Madrid. El último, ¿eh? Mañana ya no existe. Dime que sí y lo envolvemos ahora mismo.
Setenta y nueve, no, caballero. Setenta y siete P, y ahí termina mi generosidad salmantina. Es una cifra justa, usted lo sabe tan bien como yo. Diga que sí y guardo la pieza esta misma tarde.
Oh, oh... 5 P, and only because you have a kind face.
Let us be civilised: 22 P.
Thirty-two. You moved, I moved. Don't get used to it.
A gracious step, señor. I move as well: 26 pesetas. Modest, yes, but honest — I know this card to the last copy printed. Shall we shake hands and keep the afternoon pleasant?

¡Amigo, amiga, come close! Paco here, Nando there — look, look: La Heroína del Dos de Mayo, pure fuego. For you, 73 P. And quickly, eh? Another team was just sniffing around and offered us much more. We like your faces better. Decide now, ¿sí?

"¡Amigo, amigo! Paco, show the lady—"

"—the Barca del Estanque! Rare, beautiful, corners like glass. Four P and it's yours."

"Four! A gift, truly."

"But quick, quick — the police... I mean, our taxi, it's waiting outside, motor running. Decide now, eh? We vanish like smoke!"
You move, I move. 31 P.
I think 27 P is more appropriate.
Nando, he's robbing us! Fine, 4 P.

Condición perfecta, sí — como todas las que guardo en mi caja fuerte. Pero el precio no cambia por el adjetivo: 22 P, señor. Es una cifra justa, y yo no regateo. ¿La cerramos como personas civilizadas?

¡Nando, que no escucha! Amigo, five, four — we're practically family already. El Frutero de Argumosa, four, and Paco throws in the story for free: abuela painted the fruit herself. Four. Case closes in one minute, we have a train, ¿sí?

¡Amigo, amigo! Paco here, Nando there — come, come! Look: San Isidro, beautiful, rare, yours for 73 pesetas. And listen, the team at the next stall is already reaching for it, but we like your face better. Decide quick, before my brother's conscience sells it to them, eh?

¡Ay, cincuenta! Nando, did you hear? — I heard, hermano, my heart cracked. Look, 63 P, and we shake hands right now. And listen, amigo: this is the last one in all of Madrid, I swear on my mother's paella. Nobody else has it. Say sí before Paco changes his mind.

¡Cuarenta y dos! Nando, tápate los oídos, que se nos pone rojo. Mira, amigo, por ser tú, por los viejos tiempos y porque mi hermano tiene el corazón blando: 64 P y El Marqués sale ya envuelto. Un amigo de Sevilla lo quiere, pero tú primero. ¿Hecho?
Setenta y ocho, de acuerdo, caballero. Trato hecho. La pieza entra esta misma tarde en el álbum, junto a las demás del barrio. Ha negociado usted como un señor. Un placer, y vuelva cuando guste.

Let us be civilised: 23 P.
Fair is fair indeed — 28 pesetas. You descend one step, I ascend one; very courteous of us both. Mercado de la Paz belongs in my Salamanca album, señor, and I do pay properly for what I love.

"Nueve? Señora, you are too generous—"

"—but we are men of our word, Paco! Four P we said, four P it stays!"

"The Barca del Estanque, yours for four. Take it before our taxi leaves without us, eh? ¡Vámonos!"

¡Ay, cuarenta y cinco! Nando, ¿oíste? — Lo oí, hermano, casi lloro. Mira, amigo: 63 pesetas y la San Isidro es tuya. Los del puesto de al lado ya vienen con el dinero en la mano, pero tú nos caes mejor. Dilo rápido, que mi hermano es débil.

¡Ay, cincuenta y seis! Nando, one P apart — one! — Paco, finish it: 57 P, and that is our last word, amigo. No more dancing. The team next door is waving at us right now, but we like your face better. Say sí, or we pack the suitcase and go.
